title: Georgia AG and GBI return roughly $151,000 in crypto stolen from Columbia County scam victim
date_note: The Attorney General's release is dated 23 November 2026 and gives no earlier day; Valdosta Today published it on 24 November.
org: Georgia Attorney General's Office / Georgia Bureau of Investigation
geo_basis: county named in the source; centre of county used, victim's city not stated
summary: Georgia's Attorney General's release says the Georgia Bureau of Investigation, helped by the Columbia County Sheriff's Office, traced and seized roughly $151,000 in stolen cryptocurrency, and the Attorney General's White Collar and Cyber Crime Unit returned it to a Columbia County investment fraud victim. The release says she was contacted through LinkedIn and sent a link to a fraudulent app marketed as the "Onchain" app.
plain: Georgia authorities say roughly $151,000 in stolen crypto was traced, seized and returned to a Columbia County woman who was contacted on LinkedIn and sent to a fraudulent app.
exec: Georgia authorities report returning roughly $151,000 in crypto to a victim of an investment scam that began on LinkedIn.
action: The Georgia Attorney General's release urges scam victims to report to local law enforcement, Operation Shamrock, the FBI's IC3 (ic3.gov) and the FTC (reportfraud.ftc.gov).
impact: Roughly $151,000 in stolen crypto was traced, seized and returned, per the Attorney General's release.

evidence.quote: worked to trace and seize a portion of the stolen crypto – totaling roughly $151,000.

validation.note: The Georgia Attorney General's own release was read in this run; Valdosta Today relays it.

review.note: date, roughly 151,000, LinkedIn/Onchain, advice checked against AG release; evidence quote found on Valdosta Today
